title: How many sticks does a number need?
description: The sticks in two numbers are counted digit by digit. Then exactly two sticks are added to the second number to make bigger numbers. Keeko raises the doubt that the digit one uses a single stick.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the sticks digit by digit from the fixed pattern, then look for digit changes that add exactly the sticks allowed. Watch for students who draw the digit one with a single stick.

source: Count the sticks in 5108 and in 42,019. Then add exactly two sticks to 42,019 to make bigger numbers.
video_script.why: The child has met digits drawn with sticks, and now counts the sticks in numbers and adds sticks to make bigger numbers.
video_script.substitution: Count the sticks digit by digit; look for digit changes whose added sticks total exactly two.
video_script.anchor: digits drawn with sticks as on a calculator, showing 5108 and 42,019
video_script.wrong_answer: the digit one uses a single stick
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko draws the digit one with a single stick and so counts one stick fewer for every one in a number.
video_script.payoff_line: Count the sticks digit by digit, then find the changes that add exactly two

final_answer.value: 5108 needs 20 sticks; 42,019 needs 23; for example 42,049, 42,078 and 92,019
final_answer.spoken: twenty sticks and twenty three sticks, with bigger numbers such as forty two thousand forty nine

maths_rules: one stick added: 0 to 8, 1 to 7, 9 to 8; any two give 42,879, 42,818 or 42,078
two sticks added to one digit: 1 to 4, 2 to 8, 4 to 9 give 42,049, 48,019, 92,019
a new digit 1 uses exactly two sticks, so 1,42,019 is also bigger
the slip: the digit 1 is drawn with one stick, so 5108 would need 19
video_script.design: One idea: count the sticks digit by digit, then look for changes that add exactly two sticks. The stick digits stay in the anchor; the working band builds each count. Keeko's doubt: the digit one uses a single stick.
open_questions: The worklist also lists 1,42,019 (a new digit one in front). The video shows it in step three but keeps it out of the final answer line, which gives examples only.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>Four, two, zero, one and nine take four, five, six, two and six sticks, which makes twenty three.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, change one digit to add one stick.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Zero becomes eight, one becomes seven and nine becomes eight, and each adds one stick.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Any two of these changes add two sticks.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Zero and one give forty two thousand eight hundred seventy nine.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Zero and nine give forty two thousand eight hundred eighteen.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>One and nine give forty two thousand seventy eight.
<bookmark mark='m7'/>In the last two, the nine drops, but a higher place rises.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Count the sticks digit by digit, then find the changes that add exactly two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five thousand one hundred eight needs twenty sticks, and forty two thousand nineteen needs twenty three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two more sticks can make forty two thousand forty nine and forty two thousand seventy eight.
Ninety two thousand nineteen is one more.
